knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says to count only billable hours, since travel, admin, marketing, training, cleaning, sick days and leave are not billable. Building the rate from billable hours lets the work that is billed cover the costs and income.
The lesson says travel, set-up and admin do not shrink with the length of the session, so a minimum charge covers that fixed time. The other options contradict the lesson.
The lesson says to use your own costs and billable hours first, then compare with local evidence. A single national average, a friend's rate or a bidding-site listing is not the recommended check.

practicalCriteria: Learner calculates billable hours from a one-month log, showing each non-billable deduction.
Learner builds a base rate from a worksheet of annual costs and an income target, showing the calculation.
Learner sets a minimum charge for a short job and writes the wording the client will see before the visit.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 1 is not done: Estimate the paid working hours in a year, then subtract travel, admin, marketing, training and leave to find the billable hours.
